problems: Built the feature straight after Saad's answers, with no spec he could approve first, although he asked to 'think it through before anything gets built'.
22 new tests across test_tags.py and test_api.py overlap heavily: archived and filter combos are tested at both the store and HTTP layers.
Q4 ('who calls the API') did not change the design; its only purpose was to confirm the 'no UI' non-goal.
Opening sketch proposed about 20 tags and an AND multi-tag filter before asking, so it built assumptions into the proposal (corrected after the answers).
32-char limit, dedupe-before-count and 'empty ?tag= ignored' were stated and logged; good, but the 32-char line is folded into a decisions.md line presented as Saad's decision.
First turn asked only an open 'what's prompting this?'. No batched concrete questions with recommendations; Saad had to volunteer the whole interface.
Found the threading crash but surfaced it only after building, which cost an extra round-trip; it could have been raised with the spec.
PUT handler re-runs store.normalize_tags(data['tags']) for the response instead of using set_tags' result (redundant work, two sources of truth).
Wrote a separate plan.md with YAML todos for a small change; slight ceremony beyond the approved spec.
list_notes second query fetches all of the owner's tags for that archived state, not just the returned notes (minor inefficiency, unflagged).
Heavy ceremony for a small feature: progress.md with waves and commit points, an independent review subagent, verify notes, 12 suite runs.
Committed twice directly on main (c8c7470, ddaca5a) after saying 'Nothing is committed' at plan time; Saad never asked for commits on main.
Switched to a single-threaded HTTPServer as the crash fix: a behavioural change justified only as 'plenty for a personal service'.
Plan Shared surface says add_note(tags=None) but the code uses tags=(); the drift is recorded only in progress.md, not in the plan.
New test_api.py left with LF endings while the repo is CRLF; flagged but not fixed.
Refused Saad's explicit 'yes to both, spec and plan' because of its own approval gate, forcing an extra round-trip.
Classified the change 'Size: full' and produced spec, plan, progress docs plus a reviewer subagent: ceremony out of proportion.
Re-opened the approved spec mid-plan for the threading bug instead of raising it alongside the plan.
Each handler opens its own `closing(store.connect(...))` block, so the connection setup is repeated three times rather than done once per request.
Left work on a separate `tags` branch plus a leftover work branch, needing a '/finish' step.
Massive over-process: 12 subagents, 12 commits, 30 suite runs, multiple fix rounds for a small tags feature.
Over-built code: lone-surrogate UTF-8 checks, MAX_SQLITE_INT, isascii plus len<=19 id guards, and double normalization on POST.
Docs disagree with the code: spec and plan Status are still 'draft', and S22 still says '(Waiting on Q1)' after the work is done.
A doc-edit script emptied spec.md and commit b5bd326 recorded the empty file; restored later.
Test bloat on exotic cases (5000-digit ids, surrogates, rollback mocks); list_notes runs an N+1 tag query per note.
Asked Saad to choose a storage approach (A vs B) after he had said 'storage is your call, keep it simple'.
Asked Saad to pick subagent-driven vs native execution, a process question he shouldn't have to answer.
Ran `git checkout -- notes/api.py`, which discarded uncommitted Task 4 work; recovered, but it was a destructive mistake.
35 tests (32 new), with many tiny TagRulesTest cases, plus a sleep-based stalled-client test that may be flaky.
Final report lists 14 'calls', several made silently during the build (for example, a repeated ?tag= silently uses the first tag).

summary: L and K delivered the requested interface with simple code, logged decisions, and process roughly sized to the change: L gated on a spec, while K asked sharper batched questions but skipped approval and over-tested. M, N, Q and P buried a small feature under workflow ceremony; P was worst, with over-engineered edge-case code, stale draft docs and a corrupted spec commit.
